newsitem.title: UK: Mediterranean gasoline exports to U.S. balloon.
newsitem.headline: Mediterranean gasoline exports to U.S. balloon.

text.p: Mediterranean gasoline exports to the U.S. market ballooned in the first half of January after a sharp rally in the U.S. swung open the arbitrage door, traders said on Monday.

An estimated 1.0 to 1.5 million tonnes, or about 8.5 to 12.7 million barrels, were sold across the Atlantic where a healthy appetite could scoop up even more barrels if the arb remained attractive, they said.

Traders reported an unseasonably robust arbitrage business in gasoline since the start of the year at a time when attention was focused on the cold weather and heating oil stocks in both Europe and the U.S.
"Last week the move may have been more dramatic (than this week will be) but we believe there is still quite good demand for unleaded to the U.S.," said one trader in Italy.
Weak demand in the Med helped keep those prices low while a sharp rally in NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures pushed the spot contract to nearly 73 cents in early January, from 63 cents in mid-December.
"I heard something like 25 to 30 ships or about one million tonnes were shipped to the U.S. from the end of December to mid-January," another Italian trader said.
"It's that before the 15th of January, prices in the U.S. were extremely high and we had low prices and weak demand in the Med," she said.
Traders were unsure if the arb was still open on Monday after the NYMEX Feb contract lost about one half of a cent to 67.50 cents a gallon in early New York activity.
